description: BFMT* (Bidirectional Fast Marching Tree) runs FMT* from both ends over one batch of random samples. One tree marches outward from the start in order of cost-to-come; the other marches from the goal in order of cost-to-go. The trees take turns, and a sample that both trees reach joins them into a path. By default BFMT* stops once the node it just expanded was already expanded by the other tree, and returns the cheapest join; this keeps FMT*'s *asymptotic optimality* (the cost converges in probability to the optimum as the batch grows). A faster mode stops at the first meeting, which in general is not the cheapest path through the batch.

papers.authors: Joseph A. Starek, Javier V. Gomez, Edward Schmerling, Lucas Janson, Luis Moreno, Marco Pavone
papers.title: An Asymptotically-Optimal Sampling-Based Algorithm for Bi-directional Motion Planning
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
